name: Reminders
plain: Reads and edits the Reminders app's lists.
meaning: Task lists reveal chores, errands, health habits and relationships.

android.note: No system-wide reminders store; alarms use AlarmClock intents (SET_ALARM normal permission) and Google Tasks has no public provider

limits.headline: Can see and change your Reminders lists on iPhone; Android has no shared list
limits.user_action: You tap Allow Full Access when a task app asks for Reminders
can: Add, tick off and change reminders (iPhone)
Set an alarm on Android with a normal permission
cannot: Use an add only mode on iPhone; there is none
See Reminders on Android, since no system wide store exists
See Google Tasks on Android, which has no public access
limits.differs: iPhone has a Reminders store with a full access prompt; Android has none.

story.what_it_is: Lets the app read and edit your Reminders lists.

marketing.name: EventKit reminders
marketing.pitch: Apps can read and write reminders, with the permission of the person.

story.for_you: A prompt asks to access reminders. If you allow it, the app can see your to dos and add its own. Your chores, errands and medicine reminders become visible to it.
story.for_makers: A task app can plug into the system list so people do not need a second one. It can also add reminders for the app's own tasks. Lists tell a lot about a person's life, so the permission is strict.

use_cases.example: A to do app syncs with your Reminders so tasks show in both.
A medicine app adds daily dose reminders.
A grocery list app shares a shopping list with family.
A homework planner adds due dates.
A habit app adds a daily walk reminder.
A home app adds chores for the family.
A project tool turns tasks into reminders.

story.android_note: Android has no shared reminders store. Alarms use system intents and Google Tasks has no public provider.
story.ios_note: iOS has no write only mode for reminders.
